parsed.headline: President Mahama inspects poultry processing plant construction in Bechem, Ghana

pages.text: President John Dramani Mahama inspected ongoing construction of the Poultry, Meat and Feed Processing Plant in Bechem, located in the Ahafo Region of Ghana. The inspection was conducted as part of the first day of the President's two-day Resetting Ghana tour of the Ahafo Region. During the visit, Mahama stated that once the factory is operational, it is projected to position Bechem as the chicken capital of Ghana and create jobs for more people. He advised local youth to enter the poultry farming industry to utilize the factory's market. The President noted that the Nkokɔ Nketenkete initiative was started to ensure a value chain for the poultry industry prior to the commencement of factory work. Mahama, who cut the sod for the project on November 27, 2025, expressed satisfaction with the progress, reporting that work has reached approximately 50 per cent completion. He commended the project's consultants, Architecture and Engineering Services Limited (AESL), for their work. The facility is expected to be ready for commissioning by the end of the first quarter of 2027. Separately, the Minister of Food and Agriculture, Eric Opoku, stated that following the launch of the Nkokɔ Nketenkete initiative under the Feed Ghana Programme, Ghana's domestic poultry production increased from 4.6 per cent to 22 per cent as of May 2026.

parsed.headline: Taiwan to increase defense spending to deter war with China

pages.text: President Lai Ching-te announced in a National Day speech that Taiwan is boosting defense spending to deter war with China. Speaking outside the Presidential Office in Taipei, Lai stated that the aim of increasing investment in national defense is to deter war rather than to provoke. He accused China of using military and grey-zone activities to change the status quo across the Taiwan Strait and warned that peace cannot be taken for granted. Beijing claims the self-governed island as part of its territory and has not ruled out using force to bring it under its control. Lai's government has allocated a record NT$1.1 trillion ($34.5 billion) for defense spending in 2027, an amount equivalent to more than 3% of the island's GDP.

parsed.headline: Winners of BRAC Bank-Samakal Literary Awards 2024-2025 announced in Dhaka, Bangladesh

pages.text: The winners of the BRAC Bank-Samakal Literary Awards for 2024 and 2025 were announced at a ceremony held at the Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel in Dhaka on October 9, 2026, according to a press release. The awards, organized by BRAC Bank and Daily Samakal, aim to promote Bangla literature and inspire writers. The ceremony featured Chief Guest Dr. Wahiduddin Mahmud, an eminent economist and adviser to the caretaker government, alongside various media and banking executives and literary figures. The Lifetime Achievement Award, which includes a Tk. 5 lakh prize, was presented to writer Prof Serajul Islam Choudhury for 2024 and novelist Selina Hossain for 2025. Other prize categories included the essay, autobiography, travel, and translation category (Tk. 3 lakh), the poetry and novel category (Tk. 3 lakh), and the Young Writer Award (Tk. 2 lakh). All winners also received a crest and citation.

For the 2024 BRAC Bank–Daily Samakal Literary Award, Abul Ahsan Choudhury won in the essay, autobiography, travel, and translation category for the book “Vidyasagar, Bankimchandra, Rabindranath and Musolman Samaj.” Anwara Syed Haq won in the poetry and novel category for “Shomoy Bohiya Gelo,” and Nizam Biswas received the Young Writer Award for “Jolmakorer Noukabaich.” For the 2025 awards, Nasreen Jahan won in the essay, autobiography, travel, and translation category for “Paloker Chinhogulo,” Shaheen Akhtar won in the poetry and novel category for “Manchitra,” and Mahbub Mayukh Rishad received the Young Writer Award for “Cyanide Phool.”

parsed.headline: Police in Khulna, Bangladesh, instructed not to travel alone at night

pages.text: Police in the Khulna district of Bangladesh have been instructed not to travel alone at night following a knife attack that seriously injured a police inspector in Khulna city. The directive was issued in an official letter signed by the superintendent of police of the District Special Branch (DSB) on the night of October 9, 2026. The letter noted that special operations are underway in the Rupsa, Terokhada, Dighalia, and Batiaghata police station areas in response to the current law and order situation and several recent incidents, including attacks by criminals on law enforcement personnel. Unit in-charges were directed to take necessary measures to ensure the personal safety of personnel engaged in special operations and other duties. Copies of the directive were sent to all relevant offices and police stations under the district police. Khulna Superintendent of Police Sarker Omar Faruk told Prothom Alo that the restriction was imposed to prevent police personnel from falling victim to muggers while returning home after duty. When asked if the directive suggested police insecurity, Faruk stated the internal letter's main purpose is to ensure no personnel fall victim to muggers. The instruction follows an incident on October 9, 2026, at approximately 2:30 a.m., when 43-year-old Police Inspector Shah Alam was attacked by muggers in front of Khulna Collegiate School on Khan Jahan Ali Road. According to police sources, Alam was traveling by rickshaw in plain clothes after conducting a special operation in Rupsa upazila when three muggers intercepted him and attempted to snatch his money and mobile phones. When he resisted, the attackers struck both his wrists with a sharp machete. Alam was rescued by police and taken to a hospital, but as his condition deteriorated, he was transferred to a private hospital in Dhaka, where he remains under treatment in critical condition.

parsed.headline: UN records approximately 280 Israeli incursion-related incidents in Syria during September

pages.text: The United Nations human rights office reported that around 280 incidents involving armed Israeli incursions into Syria were recorded during September. According to the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, this represents the highest monthly figure since the beginning of 2026. The UN stated that these figures were based on open-source monitoring.
